subject: Cascade of p95/p99 spikes - runtime GPU fragmentation suspected
messages:
From: Samir Khan <samir.khan@brightwell.com>
To: connor.obrien@redwood.ai
Cc: emily.zhao@brightwell.com
Date: Wed, 22 Mar 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent p99 spikes/503s on prod - urgent

Connor —

We're seeing recurring p99 latency spikes and a rise in 503s on the Hosted API for our account (route: /v1/generate). It started around 08:40 PDT and has happened in five short bursts since. P95 is elevated too but p99 is the real problem — some requests jump from ~120ms to 3.5s and a subset return 503.

Attached are a filtered trace sample and a heap snapshot from one of the affected nodes (heap_profile_03022.png). We also captured request IDs: 8f7a4, 8f9c2, 90a12 if that helps correlate logs. This is impacting checkout flows and we need an ETA on mitigation.

Can you confirm whether this is on your side or something on our end?

Samir
Ops Lead, Brightwell Payments
From: connor.obrien@redwood.ai <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@brightwell.com>
Cc: emily.zhao@brightwell.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 22 Mar 2028 09:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent p99 spikes/503s on prod - urgent

Samir — thanks for the quick report and attachments. I'm pulling in Runtime on-call (Rishi) and our SREs to triage immediately.

Immediate plan:
- Rishi will examine request traces + node heap to check for GPU memory fragmentation / OOM patterns.
- We'll identify affected model variant and isolate traffic (can temporarily route to a compatible variant if necessary).
- If we find persistent slab fragmentation, we have a mitigation we can apply: rolling restarts of the GPU pool + temporary increase of KV cache TTL.

I'll update within 30 minutes with diagnostics and next steps. Appreciate the request IDs — they're already helping.

—Connor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: connor.obrien@redwood.ai, sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 22 Mar 2028 09:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent p99 spikes/503s on prod - urgent

Connor / Sergio — initial triage: I looked at the traces and the heap snapshot Samir attached. Quick notes:
- There are >30 short-lived GPU OOM events across three hosts in the Brightwell pool between 08:38–09:02 PDT. The runtime reported kernel OOM then recovered by evicting KV entries and retrying, which correlates with 503s.
- Memory fragmentation signatures (numerous small free slabs, rising alloc/realloc churn) are present in the profile.
- Affected model is redwood/gpt-3o-v2-fp16@v3 (we're in the middle of a canary for a micro-optimizing kernel change).

Immediate mitigations I recommend (in order):
1) Roll affected hosts out of traffic and do rolling restarts to defragment GPU slabs (low risk, quick).
2) If restarts are insufficient, migrate Brightwell traffic to redwood/gpt-3o-v2-int8@v1 (compatible but slightly lower throughput) for 2–4 hours.
3) Increase per-tenant KV cache TTL and lower max_batch_window to reduce burst allocation pressure.

I'm spinning up an isolated canary with the int8 variant now in us-west-2 and will report perf after 10 minutes.

Rishi
Sr. Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: connor.obrien@redwood.ai <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@brightwell.com>, Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@brightwell.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 22 Mar 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Action plan & short mitigation deployed

Samir / Emily — quick update after Rishi's triage:
- Cause: GPU memory fragmentation during a kernel canary resulted in transient OOMs + KV eviction cascades, causing p99 spikes and 503s.
- Action taken: we temporarily shifted Brightwell traffic to the int8-compatible variant and performed rolling restarts on three noisy hosts.
- Immediate outcome: p99 spike frequency dropped from ~5 bursts/hr to 0–1 bursts/hr in the 20 minutes following the mitigation. P95 returned close to baseline.

Next steps we're taking:
- Monitoring for 2 hours; if stable we'll keep the int8 variant for 4–6 hours while we complete a deeper memory-defrag pass on the runtime images.
- We'll produce a postmortem with timeline and fix candidates (kernel revert vs. targeted allocator patch).
- Connor -> will schedule a 30-min readout with your infra/product leads at 11:30 PDT if that works.

Please tell me if you need an earlier bridge. We're also open to a small service credit if Brightwell prefers; I can escalate to my manager.

—Connor
From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@brightwell.com>
To: connor.obrien@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 22 Mar 2028 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Action plan & short mitigation deployed

Thanks — the temporary improvement looks promising. We still saw one ~2.4s request at 10:08 (ID 9b2d1) but overall traffic is much better.

We'd like to accept the 11:30 PDT readout and would appreciate a proposed wording for any credit/offering we can present to internal stakeholders. The checkout impact cost is material; procurement will expect clarity.

Emily
Director, Platform Reliability — Brightwell Payments
From: connor.obrien@redwood.ai <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 22 Mar 2028 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Exec sync request — Brightwell p99 bursts, potential SLA credit

Laura / Marissa / Sergio — following up on the Brightwell incident earlier today:

Summary: Brightwell experienced repeated p99 latency spikes and correlated 503s caused by GPU memory fragmentation triggered during a kernel canary. We mitigated by moving traffic to an int8-compatible variant and performing rolling restarts; immediate user-facing impact reduced significantly.

Customer asks: clarity on root cause timeline, plan for long-term fix (allocator/kernel rollback), and a proposal for a small service credit to cover business impact.

Key asks for execs:
- Can we approve a 10% one-month credit to be applied to Brightwell's next invoice? Procurement is asking for a concrete offer.
- Should we prioritize an immediate rollback of the kernel canary in us-west-2 or continue with allocator patching? Rishi thinks rollback has lowest risk/time to normalcy.
- Please join the 11:30 PDT readout with Brightwell (I will send a calendar invite).

I've attached the heap profile and request traces; INF-3492 is tracking the follow-up work.

Connor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
